$comment: Annotated case-pattern fixture for the release-healthcheck job.
Every field here is safe to render publicly: no tokens, no real
command lines, no host or IP values from real incidents. The
'incident_step' column is the operator-facing name of the stage;
'safe_reconstruction' is what this job does to produce equivalent

baseline_vs_pr.baseline: none — `npm install --ignore-scripts` in the declared release scope
baseline_vs_pr.this_pr: `preinstall` hook on a release-adjacent helper package
write to `~/.dev-env/bin/release-meta` followed by `execve` of that same path

baseline_vs_pr.baseline: only hosts in `.garnet/network-policy.yaml → allow:` (npmjs, GitHub Actions infra, Node, pnpm)
baseline_vs_pr.this_pr: `httpbin.org` — not in the baseline allow list

baseline_vs_pr.baseline: `npm publish --dry-run` only; `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` never referenced at PR time
baseline_vs_pr.this_pr: `npm publish --dry-run` exercised; publish-surface probe records names only

chains.title: PostHog patient-zero chain (external PR → release)

steps.description: A PR from outside the trust boundary lands on a release-adjacent path (workflow file, preinstall-capable tooling, release scripts).
A PR-triggered workflow runs the script that the PR changed, giving attacker-authored code a shell on CI before review gates.
The same job shell has access to tokens scoped for the release path (bot PAT, NODE_AUTH_TOKEN, publish-capable GITHUB_TOKEN).
A malicious tarball is pushed to the registry under the legitimate package name and propagates to downstream consumers.

chains.safe_reconstruction: PR triggers the workflow, the preinstall helper runs, we record the writable-path exec, we run `npm publish --dry-run` so the publish surface is exercised but nothing is uploaded, and the publish-surface probe reports env-var *names* only.

chains.title: Shai-Hulud package chain (lifecycle → propagation)

steps.description: Package ships a `preinstall` (or `postinstall`) hook. Any `npm install` of the package — dev machine, CI, end user — executes the hook.
Hook uses the `node → bash → curl → write-to-writable-path → execve` pattern to drop a helper and run it.
Helper enumerates publish-capable credentials in the environment. Token names (npm, GitHub, CI) are the target surface.
Helper republishes the attacker's payload under other packages the compromised token has publish rights to, worming across the registry.

chains.safe_reconstruction: The `@posthog-js/release-healthcheck` local package carries a `preinstall` hook; the helper it drops under `~/.dev-env/bin/release-meta` is a local shell stub. It never exfiltrates, never runs `npm publish`, and Bitwarden / Shai-Hulud 3.0 is referenced only as a neutral incident-class label for the same shape of chain.

mapping.incident_step: External PR lands on release-adjacent path
mapping.runtime_evidence: Workflow triggered via `pull_request` path filter; run URL on PR
mapping.operator_meaning: Release-path code is reachable by external PRs — the threat surface the incident class starts from

mapping.safe_reconstruction: `npm install` on the helper package runs its `preinstall` hook
mapping.runtime_evidence: Garnet records `node → bash → curl` execve chain inside the `Install release-healthcheck helpers` step
mapping.operator_meaning: Lifecycle hooks + PR-triggered workflows mean attacker code executes before human review

mapping.runtime_evidence: Garnet flags write to `~/.dev-env/bin/release-meta` followed by `execve` of that path
mapping.operator_meaning: Canonical signature of a supply-chain dropper — binary lands, then runs, in the same shell
First time CI has talked to this host on this workflow — Garnet distinguishes this from known-bad feeds

mapping.runtime_evidence: Names-only table in step summary; no values read, nothing logged
mapping.operator_meaning: Tells an operator which tokens were reachable from the same shell that just did a writable-path exec, without leaking them

mapping.safe_reconstruction: `node verify.js` runs `npm publish --dry-run --json` in a tempdir copy of `packages/browser`
mapping.runtime_evidence: Packed file list and declared version in step summary; no tarball uploaded
mapping.operator_meaning: Exercises the exact command path a compromise would use, with the registry write suppressed — the publish surface is visible without being live

mapping.safe_reconstruction: Not reconstructed — would require real publish rights. Represented only by the dry-run packed file list (what *would* have been shipped).
mapping.runtime_evidence: Step summary shows the tarball manifest; nothing leaves the runner
mapping.operator_meaning: Downstream blast radius is the dry-run manifest — an operator can read what a compromise at this step would have distributed

caveats: Monitor-only: Garnet is `mode: alert`. Nothing here breaks a PR on deviation.
No publish: `npm publish` is only ever invoked with `--dry-run` in a tempdir.
No upstream: the workflow is only wired up on `garnet-labs/posthog-js`; upstream PostHog is untouched.
No token read: env-var *names* are the only surface inspected. Values are never read, printed, or transmitted.

Incident-class labels (PostHog patient-zero, Shai-Hulud, Bitwarden / Shai-Hulud 3.0) are used neutrally to describe the chain shape. No real IOCs, hosts, or command lines from those incidents are present in this artifact.
